name_note: Almost all published work uses the older name Coprococcus comes; the species was moved to the new genus Allocoprococcus in 2026.

sentences.text: Allocoprococcus comes, long known as Coprococcus comes, was moved in 2026 into the new genus Allocoprococcus after genomic analysis separated it from Coprococcus sensu stricto.
It is a member of the Lachnospiraceae in the human gut that takes up acetate, propionate and butyrate and incorporates them into valerate and caproate.
In one survey of gut isolates it was the only tested species that produced caproate, and it encodes a second thiolase with increased activity on butyryl-CoA.
It has been described as an acetate-producing species, and its relative abundance rose in older adults with frailty given low-methoxy pectin.
A comparison of Dutch and South-Asian Surinamese residents reported this species enriched in the Dutch gut.
